context.body: Sabbath is described as a sign between God and Israel through their generations and is connected to creation-rest language.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: A recurring practice now functions as sign, distinguishing it from one-time signs such as the rainbow or circumcision initiation.
observations.label: Sabbath as a covenant sign: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Keep · rest visible within its covenant claim.
observations.label: Sabbath as a covenant sign: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Israel · Sabbath sign · Keep · rest · Creation rest remembered
observations.label: Relationships named in Exodus 31:12–17

payload.posture: Read Exodus 31:12–17 as its own sinai covenant setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places Creation rest remembered inside this covenant setting without turning it into a definition for every covenant passage.
payload.title: Sabbath as a covenant sign
